traitReasons.pavedEfficiency: Road R1's narrow tires, rigid chassis and road-focused cockpit prioritize efficient paved riding.
traitReasons.mixedSurface: Road R1 can tolerate limited rough surfaces, but that is not its primary design target.
traitReasons.technicalTerrain: Road R1 lacks the tire volume, geometry and suspension intended for technical trail riding.
traitReasons.distanceEfficiency: Its riding position and road-oriented rolling setup are built around sustained distance efficiency.
traitReasons.climbingCapability: Low rolling losses and an efficient road drivetrain suit sustained paved climbing.
traitReasons.comfortControl: Road R1 favors efficiency and direct response over rough-terrain control and impact isolation.
traitReasons.cargoUtility: The current Road R1 reference has no dedicated cargo or utility architecture.
traitReasons.allWeather: Disc brakes help, but the reference bike is not a dedicated all-weather utility platform.
traitReasons.maintenanceSimplicity: A rigid frame/fork avoids suspension service, although the road drivetrain and hydraulic brakes still require maintenance.
traitReasons.suspensionCapability: Road R1 is intentionally rigid and has no suspension travel.

generalTradeoffs: Less impact isolation on rough surfaces

traitReasons.pavedEfficiency: MTB M1 can ride pavement, but wide tires, suspension and trail geometry trade some paved efficiency for control.
traitReasons.mixedSurface: Large-volume tires and trail-oriented geometry cope well with changing and rough surfaces.
traitReasons.technicalTerrain: Full suspension, trail geometry, wide tires and strong braking are built around technical terrain control.
traitReasons.distanceEfficiency: It can cover distance, but the trail setup is not optimized for sustained paved-speed efficiency.
traitReasons.climbingCapability: Wide gearing and traction support steep climbing, though the platform prioritizes trail capability over road efficiency.
traitReasons.comfortControl: Suspension, wide tires, flat-bar leverage and a dropper give strong control on uneven terrain.
traitReasons.cargoUtility: The current MTB M1 reference has no dedicated rack/cargo architecture.
traitReasons.allWeather: Hydraulic discs and off-road tires suit changing conditions better than the Road R1 reference, without making it a utility bike.
traitReasons.maintenanceSimplicity: Fork, rear shock, linkage pivots and dropper post add service complexity.
traitReasons.suspensionCapability: MTB M1 provides both front and rear suspension for rough-terrain wheel control.

traitReasons.pavedEfficiency: Urban U1 rolls efficiently on streets and cycle paths, while its upright position and utility tires prioritize practical control over maximum road speed.
traitReasons.mixedSurface: Medium-volume city tires and stable geometry tolerate rough paths and imperfect pavement, but the bike is not built for technical trail terrain.
traitReasons.technicalTerrain: Urban U1 is a rigid utility bicycle without trail geometry, suspension or off-road tires.
traitReasons.distanceEfficiency: The upright position is comfortable and practical for everyday distance, but creates more aerodynamic drag than Road R1.
traitReasons.climbingCapability: The internal-gear drivetrain provides useful everyday ratios, while the heavier utility platform is not optimized for fast or very steep climbing.
traitReasons.comfortControl: Upright geometry, swept bars, ergonomic grips and medium-volume tires prioritize visibility, easy handling and everyday comfort.
traitReasons.cargoUtility: The integrated rear rack, stable utility chassis and everyday accessory architecture are specifically intended for carrying normal commuting and shopping loads.
traitReasons.allWeather: Full fenders, protected chain, integrated lights and hydraulic disc brakes make poor-weather everyday use a core design goal.
traitReasons.maintenanceSimplicity: The internal-gear hub and full chain guard reduce exposed drivetrain maintenance, while the rigid frame and fork avoid suspension servicing.
traitReasons.suspensionCapability: Urban U1 is intentionally rigid; comfort comes from position and tire volume rather than suspension travel.

generalStrengths: Low-exposure drivetrain and simple rigid chassis
generalTradeoffs: Lower high-speed efficiency than Road R1
Heavier and less performance-focused than minimalist sport bikes

traitReasons.pavedEfficiency: Gravel G1 keeps a drop-bar riding position and efficient rigid chassis, while wider mixed-surface tires trade a little paved speed for versatility.
traitReasons.mixedSurface: Wide gravel tires, stable all-road geometry and a rigid but terrain-tolerant chassis are centered on pavement-to-gravel transitions.
traitReasons.technicalTerrain: Gravel G1 can handle rough roads and moderate off-road surfaces, but lacks the suspension, tire volume and trail geometry of MTB M1.
traitReasons.distanceEfficiency: Drop bars, efficient rolling geometry and multiple hand positions support long all-road rides.
traitReasons.climbingCapability: A low-mass rigid platform and wide-range 1× gearing support sustained paved and gravel climbing.
traitReasons.comfortControl: Wider tires, longer all-road geometry and flared drops add control on broken surfaces while preserving a performance-oriented posture.
traitReasons.cargoUtility: Frame and fork mounts support light touring or bikepacking equipment, but Gravel G1 is not a dedicated cargo bicycle.
traitReasons.allWeather: Disc brakes, larger tire volume and accessory mounts make mixed-weather riding practical, though full fenders and integrated lighting are not part of this reference bike.
traitReasons.maintenanceSimplicity: The rigid frame/fork avoids suspension service, while the exposed derailleur drivetrain still requires normal cleaning, wear checks and adjustment.
traitReasons.suspensionCapability: Gravel G1 is intentionally rigid; rough-surface compliance comes primarily from tires, frame/fork behavior and rider technique.

generalTradeoffs: Not as fast on smooth pavement as Road R1
Not intended for technical trails like MTB M1
Less cargo and weather integration than Urban U1
